Task-fMRI comparison of reward anticipation in cigarette smokers and nonsmokers, testing whether striatal responses to immediate versus equally preferred delayed rewards differ between groups.

Cross-sectional observational comparison of smokers and nonsmokers. Both groups performed the same immediate/delayed reward task. Smokers were not required to abstain and were invited to smoke before scanning. A subset completed a post-task delay-discounting reassessment.

definition.value: Signal during anticipation of immediate vs. delayed rewards (which were equally preferred) was compared in whole-brain analysis.

value: Signal was significantly greater during the anticipation of immediate reward in regions including bilateral caudate/putamen/ventral striatum, bilateral insula, bilateral prefrontal cortex/frontal pole, bilateral superior frontal gyrus, bilateral thalamus, brain stem, and anterior cingulate cortex/supplementary motor cortex.

definition.value: We compared this “immediate > delayed” effect between smokers and nonsmokers.

value: We observed a larger “immediate > delayed” effect among smokers than nonsmokers in several regions, including the right ventral striatum, bilateral caudate, right putamen, left thalamus, left hippocampus/parahippocampal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex.

description.value: Participants learned associations between colored squares and four rewards comprising two individually preference-matched immediate/delayed pairs. One trial per run was selected to be real and paid if won.

description.value: Cross-sectional fMRI study of familial AUD density and spatial working memory, vigilance, and fixation-related BOLD responses in 72 adolescents.

value: We hypothesize that youths with dense familial AUD will demonstrate BOLD activation patterns indicative of protracted neurodevelopment.
Specifically, we predict that with increasing FH density, there will be greater BOLD activation to SWM in more superior and bilateral regions than among FH negative counterparts.

description.value: Eighteen 20-second blocks alternating SWM and vigilance, with fixation rest at the beginning, middle, and end. Stimuli appeared for 1,000 ms with 1,000-ms interstimulus intervals; total duration 7 minutes 48 seconds.
Abstract line drawings appear in one of eight locations; press a button when a design repeats a location already occupied in that block. On average three of ten trials repeat, with repeats 2-back.
The same stimuli and locations are presented, but a dot appears above figures on 30% of trials; press a button when a dot appears. Controls simple motor and attention processes.
